newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latam stocks seen brighter as Wall Street settles.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen brighter as Wall Street settles.

text.p: Investors can expect a smoother ride in Latin American bourses this week as volatility easing in U.S. stock and bond markets is expected to cause less ripples in the region, analysts and traders said.

"The (Argentine) market will remain cautious, but if cash flows pick up and Wall Street steadies it may attempt a recovery to about 740 (on the blue-chip MerVal index)," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin.
Argentina's MerVal index shed 2.3 percent last week to 722.42 despite Standard & Poor's upgrade of the country's long-term foreign currency debt to BB from BB- Wednesday.
Another broker predicted volumes would recover from last week's paltry daily average of 15 million pesos ($15 million).
"People were on hold before the U.S. jobs report -- the outlook (as concerns interest rates) is not much clearer now but at least that hurdle is behind us," she added.
Brazil shares are seen steady to higher this week on continuing optimism over the privatization of the telecommunications sector, brokers said.

Brazil on Monday took a major step towards the sell-off of the telecom industry by receiving bids from groups comprising foreign and local companies for upcoming concessions to operate Band B cellular services.
Traders said share prices, particularly of Telebras and its subsidiaries, also could continue climbing if the government' s civil service reform bill passes the Lower House this week.
Last week, Brazilian shares rose 2.4 percent, closing at 9,705 points Friday.
Mexican stocks can also expect a breather at the beginning of the week after a sharp slide last week on fallout from a sell-off on the U.S. bond and stock markets, analysts said.
Nonetheless, volatility could increase again before more key U.S. data are released on Friday.
The blue chip IPC index closed at 3,752.47 points on Friday, down 2.35 percent for the week.

"I think we are relatively decoupled from Wall Street now, I feel the market has already discounted a further hike in U.S. interest rates at the May 20 Federal Open Market Committee meeting," said Alfredo Diaz, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage in Mexico City.
"Mexico's fundamentals have not changed, and shares here are cheap, so we could reach 3,800 points," he added.
Venezuelan equities were seen with brighter upside following the end of a three-week strike at telephone company CANTV, traders said.
Stiking CANTV workers returned to work Friday after the government ordered an end to their walk-out over pay-contracts, saying the dispute would be settled by third party arbitration.
The Caracas bourse's 19-share index closed Friday off 3.3 percent on the week at 6,133.83 points after five consecutive falls.
Chilean blue chips opened firm and are seen resuming their upward march this week on speculation of lower interest rates and good company first quarter earnings, said traders.
"Interest rate speculation will continue driving the market for the next 2-3 weeks, until the cut finally happens," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.

The Santiago bourse rallied last week on speculation that the Central Bank would trim interest rates by 0.25 percentage points Friday. The cut failed to materialize, but traders are betting on a change by the end of the month.

Company first quarter earnings are expected to be boosted by strong non-operating earnings as a result of the revaluation of the peso in February. The measure will help companies including power giant Endesa which have dollar-denominated debts.
Alone in the region, the 40-share IPSA index ended last week up 1.35 perecnt at 116.08 points.
